desc:
Choose two non-overlapping substrings of s, both palindromes of odd length. Non-overlapping means they share no position; they do not have to be adjacent. Return the largest possible product of their lengths.

Example: for s = "ababbb" pick aba and bbb and get 3 * 3 = 9. For s = "zaaaxbbby" pick aaa and bbb for 9.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Any single character is an odd palindrome, so a valid answer always exists. Split the string at a boundary: the best pair is (best palindrome entirely to the left) times (best palindrome entirely to the right) for some boundary.

You need, for every position, the longest odd palindrome that ends exactly there and the longest that starts exactly there. Manacher's algorithm gives the longest odd palindrome around every center in O(n).

A palindrome of length L ending at e implies one of length L - 2 ending at e - 1 (same center). Propagate this with a single sweep, then take prefix maxima from the left and suffix maxima from the right, and maximise left[i] * right[i + 1].
editorial: Run Manacher's algorithm for odd palindromes: d[c] is the number of palindromes centered at c, so the longest has length 2 d[c] - 1 and ends at c + d[c] - 1. Set endAt[c + d[c] - 1] to at least that length and startAt[c - d[c] + 1] likewise.

Shrinking a palindrome by one letter on each side keeps its center, so a palindrome of length L ending at e gives one of length L - 2 ending at e - 1. Hence sweeping right to left with endAt[i] = max(endAt[i], endAt[i + 1] - 2) yields the longest odd palindrome ending exactly at every index; the mirrored sweep gives startAt. Initialise both with 1 (single letters).

Let pre[i] be the maximum of endAt[0..i] and suf[i] the maximum of startAt[i..n-1]. The two palindromes are separated by some boundary, so the answer is the maximum of pre[i] * suf[i + 1] over i = 0 .. n-2. Total O(n) time and space. The product is at most about 9 million for n = 6000.
